slides.title: Claude Inside Hallboys
slides.subtitle: Five workflows where Claude saves hours this quarter — without changing Acumatica
slides.notes: Frame: this is not a platform pitch. We're operating inside the systems and team you already have.

slides.title: What we are not proposing
slides.body: No new ERP. No headcount cuts. No black-box AP automation. No custom build.
slides.notes: Lead with what we are NOT doing. Sarat's first objection is always 'another platform pitch'. Disarm it up front.

slides.title: Hallboys reality we are designing around
left_points: Acumatica as system of record — stays the source of truth
3-person IT team, no spare capacity for a 6-month rollout
One AP clerk processing every invoice that comes in
Claude already in use — but no shared rules or skill library
Field, office, and finance work happens on different cadences
right_points: No replacement of Acumatica or any existing system
No removal of human approval on AP, contracts, or schedule
No long onboarding — pilots run inside existing weekly meetings
No data leaves Hallboys' Claude workspace
slides.notes: Sarat needs to hear his constraints recited back before he will listen to anything new.

slides.title: Five workflows. Same team. Same systems.
slides.body: Each one targets cost, capacity, or risk — measured against today's baseline.
slides.notes: Set up the five-workflow spine. Every following slide ties back to one of these.

slides.title: Workflow 1 — Subcontractor quote comparison
slides.stat_label: Per multi-vendor bid package, estimator time (medium confidence)
slides.body: Estimator drops 3-5 sub quotes into Claude. Output: side-by-side scope, line-item deltas, missing items, risk flags. Estimator still picks the winner. Impact: cost — fewer hidden scope gaps caught after award. Capacity — estimators run more bid packages per week with the same headcount.
slides.notes: Anchor on a real number Sarat can challenge. 'Medium confidence' shows we are not bluffing the estimate.

slides.title: Workflow 2 — Equipment scheduling coordination
slides.stat_label: Avoided crew idle days from caught conflicts (medium confidence)
slides.body: Weekly schedule and equipment list go into Claude. Output: vendor overlaps, missing deliveries, dependency breaks, dates that don't match the critical path. Scheduler still owns the call. Impact: risk — one avoided idle day on a mid-size job is roughly $4-8K in crew cost.
slides.notes: Tie the save to a dollar range, not a percentage. Sarat can multiply by jobs per quarter himself.

slides.title: Workflow 3 — AP exception triage (assisted, not automated)
slides.stat_label: Same AP clerk handles more invoices without losing review quality (medium confidence)
slides.body: Every invoice still flows through Acumatica. Claude sits beside the clerk: extracts vendor, amount, PO match, scope match, flags duplicates and pricing anomalies. Clerk approves, codes, and posts in Acumatica as today. Impact: capacity — AP clerk reviews more invoices per day. Risk — fewer missed duplicates and price drifts. Not available: confirmed duplicate-rate baseline (need 90 days of AP history).
slides.notes: Hit the AP automation objection head-on. We are NOT replacing the clerk and NOT writing into Acumatica. The clerk is faster and catches more.

slides.title: Workflow 4 — Project closeout document checks
slides.stat_label: To verify a closeout package vs. the required checklist (high confidence)
slides.body: PM uploads the closeout folder. Claude returns: missing items, inconsistent dates, lien waivers without matching pay apps, warranty letters absent. PM still signs off. Impact: risk — fewer retainage delays and warranty disputes after handover. Capacity — PMs spend closeout time fixing gaps, not hunting for them.
slides.notes: Closeout is the workflow most likely to be felt immediately — Sarat will recognize the pain.

slides.title: Workflow 5 — Claude skill governance
slides.stat_label: Replacing scattered prompts across the team (high confidence)
slides.body: Today: every Claude user writes their own prompts. Result: inconsistent output, no audit trail, no reuse. Proposal: a small set of versioned skills (one per workflow above), owned by IT, used by everyone. Impact: risk — consistent outputs, no rogue prompts touching sensitive data. Capacity — new hires productive on day one.
slides.notes: This is the multiplier. Without governance, the other four workflows decay over six months.

slides.title: Pilot plan — 60 days, no platform commitment
left_points: Pick 2 of the 5 workflows (recommend: quote comparison + closeout checks)
Run beside the human owner — no system writes
Capture baseline: hours, errors caught, items missed
IT publishes v1 skills into shared workspace
Weekly 30-min review with one estimator and one PM
right_points: Add a third workflow if first two clear baseline
Sarat sees a one-page scorecard: hours saved, errors caught, prompts retired
Decision point: continue, adjust scope, or stop — no lock-in
Skill library handed to IT for ongoing ownership
Not available: training cost projection until pilot baseline lands
slides.notes: 60 days, exit at any point, no platform commitment. This is what gets a yes.

slides.title: Same team. Same systems. More throughput.
slides.body: Two workflows, 60 days, one scorecard. Decide from data, not a slide.
slides.notes: Close on the offer, not on the vision. Sarat funds pilots, not roadmaps.
